test_title: PYST 28: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 31 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

He is one of the few (1)/ manager who (2)/ consistently leads (3)/ by example. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary error in the sentence is the use of the singular noun "**manager**" after the phrase "**one of the**."
 
• In English grammar, the structure "**one of the**" must always be followed by a **plural noun** because it refers to one individual out of a larger group.
 
• Additionally, in a relative clause beginning with "**who**," the verb must agree with the antecedent (the plural noun). Therefore, "**leads**" should also be corrected to the plural form "**lead**."
 
• The core error starts in **part (2)**, where the pluralization is missing.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He is one of the few **managers who consistently lead** by example."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(1): "He is one of the few"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct as it introduces the plural selection.
 
• **(3): "consistently leads"** – This contains a subject-verb agreement error that is dependent on the noun in part (2). In many competitive exams, the section introducing the plural noun error is marked as the primary mistake.
 
• **(4): "by example."** – This is a standard idiomatic phrase and is grammatically correct.
